title: Quantify paid overhead budgets for concave rank-profile replacements
body:
Existing capped-mass certificates prove that a rank-profile change lowers every power moment, but provide no explicit allowance for added cleanup or routing. This package proves a uniform rational lower bound on that saving and a sufficient paid-admission rule: any complete added overhead bill below the certificate still yields a strictly better moment. It composes over arbitrary batches and charges positive-rank overhead by its full rank mass.

Two literal historical rank-first profiles can pay one and three additional rank-1 children, respectively, uniformly for a in [0.0017, 0.0018]. On the current PR3815/3857 full histogram, 1,775 proposed `2+2 → 1+3` exchanges would pay one extra rank-1 child; enough rank-2 children exist. This is a concrete sufficient implementation target, with no circuit realization, chronology/stock claim or new κ. The historical calibration is not a competing current supplier.

Includes the complete informal proof, exact rational certificate and read-only Git-free replay. Registered Python 3.12 checks pass, including 236 exhaustive small profile pairs, nine independent real-power enclosures, source/result corruption controls and assertion-disabled arithmetic checks. No Lean formalization or full multiplication proof is claimed.

Credit the retained ranked-pair package for the existing min-basis identity and all-exponent sign theorem, Avi Eisenberg/PR62, eumemic/PR57, Chafik Boukhalfa/PR60, Dominik Scholz/PR63 and its full predecessor notices. Current calibration credits ChaloupeMusic/PR3815, hexapode/PR3802, dataisfire/PR3734 and PR3857. Reuses the MathProof sufficient replacement-with-reserve framework. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review.

Scientific base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Overlap coverage: 565 open PR bodies, latest updated all-state records through #3860, actual related source proofs and partial Discussion HTML. No exhaustive novelty claim. The selected frontier is unchanged.
